Subject: New offer: runtime compatibility checks & publisher setup

Hi Irene,

Thanks for agreeing to help with our Azure Marketplace listing. We are preparing a managed inference offering (container + inference runtime) and want to pre-check the technical gate so the publisher account activation isn't held up. High-level asks: 

- Confirm required publisher account artifacts (tenant ID / SPN proof / contact matrix).
- Verify runtime compatibility expectations: supported GPU SKUs, container base images that are accepted by the marketplace validation, and any size/timeout constraints on ARM manifests.
- Any special requirements for co-sell enablement (multi-tenant vs. single-tenant routing, telemetry flags).

Attached is a draft manifest (nimbus-manifest-v1.json) and a short runtime notes file. Can you point us to the minimum artifacts you need to move from publisher activation -> offer creation -> technical validation?

Thanks,
Ravi Patel

Onboarding Team

From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: New offer: runtime compatibility checks & publisher setup

Hi Ravi — thanks for the starter manifest. Quick answers and next steps: 

1) Publisher artifacts: we need your Azure tenant ID, a Service Principal (SPN) owner proof (role assignment screenshot or a signed SPN manifest), and a publisher contact matrix (technical, finance, legal).

2) Runtime compatibility: for managed inference offerings we typically validate against these buckets: 
   - GPU SKUs: Standard_NC6s_v3, Standard_ND40rs_v2 (recommend to include both64-bit and 16-bit quantization paths in the manifest).
   - Container: OCI images hosted in ACR are preferred. Avoid references to experimental base images; use Ubuntu 20.04 / Debian 11 LTS base layers.
   - ARM/offer constraints: max instance disk size must be declared and any custom startup scripts flagged for review.

3) Co-sell enablement: provide a short note on tenant isolation model (single-tenant per customer vs pooled multi-tenant). For co-sell, Microsoft expects SKU-level pricing and a co-sell contact entry on the offer.

I am attaching our Redwood onboarding guide which includes a small checklist we use for publisher activation. Karthik — can you add the runtime SKU mapping and a quick note on private link requirements? Marissa — can you flag any procurement/legal items we should surface to Nimbus?

Best,
Irene Choi
Technical Program Manager, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference

Thanks Irene — quick technical checklist from infra/runtime POV: 

- GPU mapping: ND (A100) families are preferred for large models; NC-series for smaller single-GPU instances. See attached sku-mapping.csv for recommended default SKUs per model size (small/medium/large).
- Container registry: ACR with Managed Identity or SPN push access. If you plan to use a private ACR, we need the ACR resource ID and a short network diagram showing VNet/Private Endpoint usage.
- KV & secrets: use KeyVault with RBAC; do not bake secrets into images.
- Health probes/startup: marketplace validation spins up the container and runs a cold-start probe; ensure your entrypoint returns 200 on /health within 120s.
- KV cache/warmup: include a warmup script if you rely on large weights; indicate warmup latency in manifest.

I attached sku-mapping.csv and a short private-link checklist. If Nimbus wants to support quantized 4-bit runtimes, call that out explicitly — that can change the recommended SKU set.

-Karthik
Principal Infra Eng, Redwood Inference
attachments: sku-mapping.csv (csv), private-link-checklist.md (md)
